items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I consider him one of the greatest alto players I have ever heard... Fred Murphy.

ctx.x: No leader? I was supposed to be. Just thrown together and you took over.

Just thrown together, right. There was a lot of musicians out there that people have really overlooked, and I consider him one of the greatest alto players I have ever heard. And he was a real, real close copier. Well he wasn't copying because in those days Johnny Hodges was just coming along. And this guy played fantastic just like Johnny Hodges, Fred Murphy. And nothing has ever been said. Well there's so many, Dick, that you could sit out and reminisce over these guys that you know that really could play that…
Well you have to put yourself before the public. Well a lot of them don't.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Fred Murphy didn't want to, he played a few days with us until we could get a replacement.

ctx.x: Yeah there were a lot of changes in that band you told him at once I mean.

Men would come and go. No not too many in that band. My band had a lot of changes but not Troy's band. They only changed, well after yes after I left he started to change a lot of musicians to try to keep the remnants going. But when I was there it was almost a family affair because we all worked together with each other. And Scott Bagley was the only one that I could remember that dropped out and got a replacement with Herschel Evans. Because Fred Murphy didn't want to leave Dallas, Texas I tried to get Fred to…
Did he play alcohol or tennis? Alton.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: There was a great alto player in Dallas, Texas that played on the same style then that Johnny Hodges plays today. His name is Fred Murphy.

ctx.x: And not very many people have mentioned him in the books or articles.

That's right. The same way with Mr. Morad. Now there's a few others. There was a great alto player in Dallas, Texas that played on the same style then that Johnny Hodges plays today. His name is Fred Murphy. Fred Murphy. That's right. Now nobody, they failed to mention him. Then you had Buster Bailey and guys like that in those days. They failed to mention. And all those guys were great, great musicians.
Well is Buster from around here?
